html:
Raid by the shinsengumi on a group of pro-emperor, anti-shogunate samurai meeting at the Ikedaya inn in Kyoto on 8 July 1864.

The Shinsengumi, a police band serving the shogunate in Kyoto, had arrested a suspect who, under questioning, spoke of a plot by men from Choshu and allies to set fire to Kyoto, seize Emperor Komei, and strike the shogun's protectors. How real or how large the plan was is still argued. Kondo Isami led a small group into the inn, with Okita Soji and Hijikata Toshizo among the others. Several plotters were killed and more were taken.

The raid made the Shinsengumi's name. It also enraged Choshu, whose forces marched on Kyoto a few weeks later and were beaten at the Kinmon incident in August. This pushed Choshu and the shogunate toward open war, in the last years of the Tokugawa shogunate and before the Meiji Restoration.
sum: Raid by the shinsengumi on a group of pro-emperor, anti-shogunate samurai meeting at the Ikedaya inn in Kyoto on 8 July 1864.
